name: F-16C with 4 × AIM-120 (AIM-120C-DCS), flown like the DCS AI, defended by it
description: F-16C-DCSAI, with the two things the DCS bridge (version 4) adds for BLUE-1: while an enemy missile is inbound the DCS AI defends the aircraft at its full agility (beam the missile, dive, fastest speed, no shots), and the policy's commands resume when the missile is gone; and faster speed choices, 240-450 m/s, as the DCS AI flies Mach 1.3-1.5 level. Train the agent on it for DCS runs with dcs_live.py, which then turns the bridge's auto-defence on.

sources.WPN_COUNT: standard BVR loadout in this project
sources.RCS_M2: commonly cited open-source frontal estimate (≈ 1.2 m²)
sources.SPEED_CMDS: the DCS AI flew BLUE-1 level at 340 m/s at 9 km (Mach 1.12) and 400 m/s at 7 km when asked to; red in combat reaches Mach 1.5-1.75 level: the top choice is raised from 400 to 450 m/s, the others spread evenly
sources.CLIMB_FPA_LO: holds speed on a 3 km climb (measured)
sources.CLIMB_MACH: DCS climbs in 4 recorded fights (dcs_v8 v the DCS AI, 3 runs; the defender mission, 2 runs): Mach 0.82-0.88 with 220, 400 or 550 m/s commanded
sources.CLIMB_THROTTLE: fitted: with 3 km still to climb the model climbs 49-60 m/s at 10-11.5 km (DCS 50-60) and from 9 to 13 km in 89 s (DCS 75-82 s); with 1.2 km to go 23-24 m/s (DCS 22-33)
sources.TURN_BANK_MAX: dcs/turn_test.py in DCS: 90, 90 and 170 deg turns at 340 m/s and 9 km with the first route point 3 km, 1 km or not at all ahead were all flown at 45 deg of bank and 1.41 g, 1.5-1.6 deg/s
sources.AUTO_DEFEND: dcs/bvr_bridge.lua version 4, OPT autodefend: the DCS AI's own missile defence (REACTION_ON_THREAT EVADE_FIRE), which turns at more than 45 deg of bank; the simulator stands in with a beam of the missile, a 3 km dive (not below 1.5 km) and the fastest speed choice
